units.title: Econometrics: From Data to Cause and Effect
units.card: Seventeen chapters from a cloud of points to Nobel-prize methods: live regressions, Monte Carlo labs and practice with answers.

chapters.title: What Econometrics Is: Data, Models and Cause
chapters.short: A beach town where ice cream seems to cause rescues, until you hold the weather fixed, and why a coin flip beats self-selection.

chapters.title: Probability and Distributions
chapters.short: Shape seven distributions, sample thousands of draws, and watch averages of lopsided data pile into a bell.

chapters.title: Estimation and Inference
chapters.short: A machine that builds 100 confidence intervals at a time, a dartboard of estimators, and p-values you can see.

chapters.title: Simple Regression: Fitting a Line
chapters.short: Drag points and watch least squares refit with every residual drawn as a square, then meet Galton’s regression to the mean.

chapters.title: Inference in Regression
chapters.short: Draw 20,000 samples, then break the assumptions one by one to see which cause bias and which only fool the standard errors.

chapters.title: Multiple Regression and Omitted Variables
chapters.short: Leave ability out of a wage regression and watch the bias match the omitted-variable formula, then turn a 3-D regression plane.

chapters.title: Logs, Dummies and Interactions
chapters.short: Fit four log and level models to one data set, read each slope in plain English, find a career’s peak and split lines with dummies.

chapters.title: Heteroskedasticity and Robust Standard Errors
chapters.short: Fan out the noise and run 2,000 samples: classic 95% intervals fall short while robust ones hold.

chapters.title: Specification, Measurement Error and Outliers
chapters.short: Blur a variable and watch the slope shrink, drag an outlier until it bends the line, and overfit a polynomial.

chapters.title: Instrumental Variables and 2SLS
chapters.short: Use college proximity to untangle schooling from ability, then weaken and break the instrument to see 2SLS fail.

chapters.title: Panel Data: Fixed and Random Effects
chapters.short: Follow cities over time: pooled OLS gets police and crime backward until fixed effects compares each city with itself.

chapters.title: Difference-in-Differences and Event Studies
chapters.short: Break parallel trends, read event studies, and watch two-way fixed effects get the sign wrong.

chapters.title: Regression Discontinuity
chapters.short: Measure the jump at a cutoff, balance bias against noise, and catch people gaming the line.

chapters.title: Binary Outcomes: Logit, Probit and Maximum Likelihood
chapters.short: Straight lines vs S-curves for yes-or-no data, and maximum likelihood climbed by hand.

chapters.title: Time Series: Trends, Autocorrelation and Forecasting
chapters.short: From white noise to random walks: memory, spurious regressions, forecasts and cointegration.

chapters.title: VARs and GMM
chapters.short: Shock a small economy, read impulse responses, and catch a bad instrument with GMM.

chapters.title: Modern Causal Inference
chapters.short: Causal diagrams, matching, synthetic twins and double machine learning.

units.title: Game Theory: The Science of Strategy
units.card: A fourteen-chapter course in strategy, from the prisoner’s dilemma to auctions, signaling and mechanism design, with a game in every chapter.

chapters.title: Games, Players and Payoffs
chapters.short: Guess two thirds of the average against a crowd of level-k thinkers, then build games and play bots with personalities.

chapters.title: Dominance and the Prisoner’s Dilemma
chapters.short: Cross out dominated actions until a game solves itself, fall into the prisoner’s dilemma, and watch a public-goods game unravel.

chapters.title: Nash Equilibrium
chapters.short: Underline best responses to find Nash equilibria in coordination, chicken and the stag hunt, and test your feel for focal points.

chapters.title: Mixed Strategies and Zero-Sum Games
chapters.short: Play rock-paper-scissors against a bot that reads you, solve any 2×2 game by indifference, and take penalties at minimax.

chapters.title: Competition: Cournot, Bertrand and Hotelling
chapters.short: Watch Cournot firms settle into equilibrium, start a Bertrand price war, and walk ice-cream sellers to the median.

chapters.title: Sequential Games and Backward Induction
chapters.short: Build and solve game trees, unmask empty threats, deter entry with commitment, and lead a Stackelberg market.

chapters.title: Repeated Games and Cooperation
chapters.short: Run an Axelrod tournament with your own strategy, add noise and evolution, and find the δ that makes cooperation pay.

chapters.title: Incomplete Information and Bayesian Games
chapters.short: Run a used-car market where only sellers know the lemons, watch it unravel, and fix it with warranties and inspections.

chapters.title: Auctions
chapters.short: Bid against computer rivals in four auction formats, test revenue equivalence, and fall for the winner’s curse.

chapters.title: Signaling and Screening
chapters.short: Set what the good job requires and watch job seekers signal, then measure cheap talk and design a menu that sorts customers.

chapters.title: Bargaining
chapters.short: Haggle over a $100 pie with bots that differ only in patience, then find Nash’s solution as the biggest rectangle.

chapters.title: Mechanism Design and Matching
chapters.short: Run the matching algorithm behind the medical residency match, try to cheat it, and see a tax that makes honesty pay.

chapters.title: Coalitions, the Core and the Shapley Value
chapters.short: Pay each player what they add, find splits no group would reject, and discover who really holds power in a vote.

chapters.title: Evolutionary Game Theory
chapters.short: Watch hawks and doves find a balance, cooperators build kaleidoscopes on a grid, and lizards cycle like rock–paper–scissors.

units.title: Newton’s Laws of Motion
units.card: Six chapters on how everything moves, with simulations, missions, quizzes and Newton’s own words.

chapters.title: The First Law: Inertia
chapters.short: Roll a ball between Galileo’s ramps and coast a probe through space: moving things keep moving until a force changes that.

chapters.title: The Second Law: F = ma
chapters.short: Push a cart, watch its motion graphs, and drop a hammer and a feather on the Moon: F = ma.

chapters.title: The Third Law: Action and Reaction
chapters.short: Push two skaters apart and solve the horse-and-cart puzzle: every force has an equal and opposite partner.

chapters.title: Forces at Work: Free-Body Diagrams
chapters.short: Tilt a ramp till it slips, ride an elevator on a scale, race weights over a pulley, and draw free-body diagrams.

chapters.title: Momentum and Collisions
chapters.short: Crash gliders, drop eggs on pillows and split pool balls at 90°: momentum always survives, energy doesn’t.

chapters.title: Circles and Gravity: The Apple and the Moon
chapters.short: Cut a whirling string, take a banked curve, and check with Newton that the Moon falls like an apple.

units.title: The Laws of Thermodynamics
units.card: Five chapters of simulations on heat, energy, entropy, engines and absolute zero: the four laws of thermodynamics, played with.

chapters.title: Temperature and the Zeroth Law
chapters.short: Press copper, iron, granite, water and wood together and watch heat flow until they share one temperature.

chapters.title: Energy and the First Law
chapters.short: Heat, squeeze and stretch a gas, trace its P–V path, and watch ΔU = Q − W balance to the joule.

chapters.title: Entropy and the Second Law
chapters.short: Run a gas backward and watch it un-spread, nudge one atom by a billionth and watch the trick fail, and play Maxwell’s demon.

chapters.title: Engines, Refrigerators and Heat Pumps
chapters.short: Run Carnot’s ideal engine with heat and work drawn to scale, then run it backward as a heat pump, and watch a Stirling engine run on coffee.

chapters.title: Absolute Zero and the Third Law
chapters.short: Climb down a cooling ladder that never reaches the bottom, evaporate atoms into a Bose–Einstein condensate, and zoom a thermometer from picokelvins to fusion plasma.
